findings.evidence: check() forwards every extra argument unchanged: `argv = argv + list(extra)` (line 228) for the selfheal route, while CHECK_USAGE (lines 235-240) documents log_triage-only flags such as --new, --no-advance, --all-launches and --launch N. selfheal_log_check.py main() (lines 305-310) defines only a positional log_pos plus --log, --from and --to, so passing a documented triage flag to the selfheal route makes argparse fail with exit 2.
findings.suggested_investigation: Run `kotor2_logs.py check companion-selfheal --new` against a sample log and confirm the argparse error and exit code 2. Then decide whether check() should reject or strip triage-only flags for non-triage routes, or whether the usage text should say which flags apply to which route. Compare with how the engfix and luo routes already handle extra args.
findings.why_it_matters: The dispatcher is meant to be the single entry point agents use. A triage flag typed against the companion-selfheal log gives an argparse error rather than the documented behaviour. It fails loudly (non-zero exit, not silent), so the impact is usability, not correctness.
